output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Role-adaptive evidence workflows}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

A workflow is an approved activity graph. The same imported dataset can move
from analysis to modeling to review without copying evidence or losing source
row lineage.

```{r}
library(rclaimlab)
set.seed(2026)
frame <- data.frame(
  age = sample(18:70, 120, TRUE),
  hours = round(rnorm(120, 40, 8), 1),
  group = rep(c("A", "B"), 60),
  outcome = factor(ifelse(seq_len(120) %% 3 == 0, "event", "reference"))
)
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
write.csv(frame, path, row.names = FALSE)
dataset <- import_dataset(dataset_source("local", path))

analyst <- workflow_from_dataset(
  dataset, "data_analyst", predictors = c("age", "hours")
)
analyst_run <- run_workflow(approve_workflow(analyst))

scientist <- continue_workflow(
  analyst_run, "data_scientist", outcome = "outcome",
  predictors = c("age", "hours"), slice_by = "group", analysis = "glm"
)
scientist_run <- run_workflow(approve_workflow(scientist))

reviewer <- continue_workflow(scientist_run, "model_reviewer")
reviewer_run <- run_workflow(approve_workflow(reviewer))

as.data.frame(reviewer_run)
```

Approvals are required before execution. Subgroup results are suppressed below
the configured minimum and are labeled as review signals. They are not a
fairness certification. The reviewer must explicitly approve or request
revision in the workflow receipt.
